cookie-cone-shell-ice-cream-type-wafer-o.title: Cookie, cone shell, ice cream type, wafer or cake

content.title: About
content.content: A cookie cone shell is a crunchy dessert that holds a scoop of ice cream, covered with a wafer or cake layer. This product combines a sweet, creamy filling with a crisp shell, making it a popular choice during the summer and in food‑court menus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cone shells originated in Italy in the early 1920s as “gelato in cono”.
The wafer layer is usually made from a mixture of wheat flour, sugar and eggs, while the cake layer uses a lighter batter with leavening agents.
More than 30 ice‑cream flavors are used in cone desserts, ranging from classic vanilla to exotic mango and lavender honey.
Cookie‑cones are often decorated with chocolate glaze, nuts, berries or caramel sauces.
In some countries the cone dessert is served with an extra “plus” sauce on the side for drizzling.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Ice cream, especially dairy‑based, provides calcium important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cream and milk used in ice cream are rich in vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the cookie and fats from the ice cream rapidly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Mood boost
items.content: Sweet desserts stimulate serotonin production, improving mood.

items.title: Probiotic presence
items.content: Some ice‑cream varieties are made with live cultures, supporting gut microbiota.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy‑based ice cream may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Nut and gluten allergies
items.content: The cookie often contains nuts and wheat flour, which can be problematic for allergic individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of cookie and ice cream makes the product calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Melting in heat
items.content: When stored in warm conditions the ice cream can melt, affecting texture and taste.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Keep the cookie‑cone frozen until serving. Allow it to sit at room temperature for 5‑10 minutes before eating so the ice cream softens slightly. Top with chocolate sauce, nuts, berries or a sprinkle of cookie crumbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the product in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, keep it in an airtight container to prevent absorption of other odors. Do not leave the cone at room temperature for more than 30 minutes after removal from the freezer.

content.title: About
content.content: The fried fish sandwich is a fast‑food item consisting of a bun filled with a piece of breaded and deep‑fried fish, often topped with sauce, lettuce, and other vegetables. It has been a popular quick‑serve snack in the United States since the late 18th century.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fried fish sandwich was introduced in 1793 at one of the earliest American fast‑food establishments.
Traditionally white fish such as cod or pollock is used, though regional variations may feature other species.
In the U.S. it is commonly served with tartar sauce or a lemon‑mayonnaise dressing.
Some countries refer to a similar product as a “fish burger,” where the fish is formed into a patty.
The rise of plant‑based alternatives in the 2020s led to vegan versions made from soy or pea protein.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fried fish provides a complete source of animal protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: When fatty fish such as salmon is used, the sandwich can supply heart‑healthy omega‑3s.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Selenium and iodine in fish contribute to thyroid health and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the bun and fats from the fish offers a fast source of energy.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories and saturated fat, which may be undesirable in excess.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish or seafood.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Fish can contain mercury or other heavy metals; sourcing from reputable suppliers is recommended.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Condiments often contain high sodium levels, which can affect blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten hot, split in half. It pairs well with fresh lettuce, pickles, tomato slices, and a squeeze of lemon. For a lighter option, use a whole‑grain bun or bake the fish instead of frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich should be refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Keep the fried fish in an airtight container to prevent odor absorption. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer rather than a microwave to retain crispness.

ham-prepackaged-or-deli-luncheon-meat.title: Ham, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat (1005)

content.title: About
content.content: Ham is a ready‑to‑eat meat product made from pork (sometimes turkey) that is boiled, smoked or baked, then sliced and packaged. It is sold as whole pieces, sliced deli meat, or ready‑to‑serve portions and is commonly used in sandwiches, salads and snack platters.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ham originated in medieval Europe as a method of preserving pork.
Traditional Dutch “germeld” and American “deli ham” differ in smoking technique and spice blends.
Ham is often served as “medallions” – small round slices that are convenient for appetizers.
Low‑sodium ham varieties are marketed for people watching their salt intake.
Ham can be made from different pork cuts: hind leg, shoulder or loin.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Ham provides about 18–20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of zinc and iron
items.content: These minerals help immune function and oxygen transport.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ham contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains creatine
items.content: Creatine in ham may aid physical endurance and muscle performance.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Most ham contains 800–1500 mg of sodium per 100 g, which can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Nitrites are often added for color and shelf life; excessive intake may be harmful.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork proteins.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Ham contains saturated fats, so intake should be limited in cardiovascular disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham can be eaten sliced in sandwiches, added to salads, used in hot dishes (pizza, pasta) or served as a snack with cheese and fruit. For a milder flavor, briefly warm it in a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ham in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +2–+4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Freeze in portion‑size bags for longer storage, though texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken and cheese corn taco is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a corn tortilla filled with seasoned grilled chicken, melted cheese, and often topped with sauces, vegetables, and spices. The corn tortilla gives a light, slightly sweet flavor and a soft texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas have been used in Mexico for over 3,000 years.
Traditional chicken marinades include chili, lime, and garlic.
Cheese in Mexican tacos is often a meltable cheddar or queso fresco.
Tacos are typically folded in half to keep the filling inside.
Tacos gained widespread popularity in the United States in the 1920s with the rise of Mexican restaurants.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: Chicken contains niacin and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Fiber from corn tortilla
items.content: Corn tortilla contributes dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with modest cheese and without excess oil, the taco can be relatively low in saturated fat.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese and ready-made sauces can be high in salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chicken and cheese tacos can be calorie‑dense, especially when extra sauces or toppings are added.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked chicken can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla, place grilled chicken pieces inside, sprinkle with shredded cheese, and add sauce, fresh veggies, guacamole or sour cream as desired. Serve immediately while the cheese is still melty.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover tacos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tortillas in a dry place, and chicken and cheese refrigerated. Reheat until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75 °C.

tea-iced-brewed-black-decaffeinated-pre-.title: Iced Brewed Black Decaffeinated Tea Sweetened with Low‑Calorie Sweetener

content.title: About
content.content: This iced brewed black tea is decaffeinated and pre‑sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener. It retains the characteristic aroma and flavor of black tea while lacking the stimulating effect of caffeine, making it suitable for evening consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea undergoes full oxidation, giving it a deep color and robust taste.
Decaffeination is usually performed by water or CO₂ methods, preserving most beneficial compounds.
Sweetening with low‑calorie agents such as stevia or erythritol reduces calories without added sugar.
Iced brewed tea is often served over ice, providing a refreshing beverage in warm weather.
Ready‑to‑drink technology allows the product to retain flavor and freshness for several months.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Black tea is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Flavonoids may improve vascular function and help lower blood pressure.

items.title: Caffeine‑free
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes the drink safe for individuals sensitive to stimulants.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Low‑calorie sweetening allows a sweet taste without excess calories.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Iced tea contributes to daily fluid intake.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: Tannins can reduce iron absorption when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain low‑calorie sweeteners may cause digestive discomfort in some people.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the iced tea chilled, with or without ice. It can be added to cocktails, smoothies, or used as a base for fruit‑infused drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.
